title: From Hook to Dashboard
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI Agent Skills
Token Usage Measurement
Hooks
JSONL Logs
Usage Analytics
description: Step-through left-to-right flowchart that follows one skill-run event through six stages: the skill runs, a skill usage hook records the start, a stop hook records the result, one line is appended to a JSONL usage log, a Python analytics script groups the log by skill, and a token usage dashboard reports tokens and elapsed time. Clicking a node shows its definition and what the example event looks like at that stage.

educational.topic: Measuring skill token usage with hooks, logs, and dashboards
learningObjectives: Summarize how a single skill-run event travels from a hook, into a log file, and out as a dashboard metric.
Explain why the usage log is append-only and why it is storage rather than computation.
State that a token usage dashboard reports elapsed time separately from token counts.
prerequisites: Knows what a token is and why token use is limited
Has read the definitions of skill usage hook, stop hook, and JSONL usage log

pedagogical.pattern: Step-through worked example with concrete data
pedagogical.teachingStrategy: One example event is followed through every stage, and its concrete form (record, log line, grouped total, dashboard row) is shown at each step
keyQuestions: At which stage does a skill run first leave a trace?
Why does the dashboard show elapsed time as well as tokens?
commonMisconceptions: A log file by itself reveals which skills are expensive
The time a skill takes and the tokens it consumes are the same measurement
assessmentOpportunities: Write a three-sentence summary of the path from a skill run to a dashboard row and check it against the six stages
